question: A stakeholder wants Claude to read scanned engineering drawings and return exact millimeter measurements for manufacturing tolerances. How should the solutions architect set expectations about this vision use case?
options: A) Confirm that Claude's vision accuracy is unaffected by image resolution or scan quality, ensuring consistent measurements across all scenarios.
B) Confirm that Claude can read pixel-level measurements directly from any scanned drawing, ensuring guaranteed manufacturing-grade precision.
C) Explain that Claude lacks image processing capabilities, so drawings must be manually transcribed into text by staff before analysis.
D) Explain that Claude can describe and reason about visual content, but exact measurements should be verified with dedicated tools.
correct_answers: D) Explain that Claude can describe and reason about visual content, but exact measurements should be verified with dedicated tools.
explanations: Incorrect. Image resolution and scan quality can affect how accurately Claude interprets visual details, so its vision accuracy is not independent of these factors.
Incorrect. Claude does not guarantee pixel-level measurements with manufacturing-grade precision, which overstates its vision capabilities for this use case.
Incorrect. Claude does support image input and can reason about visual content, so manual transcription into text is not required; this understates its actual capabilities.

Correct. Claude can describe and reason about visual content, but it is not a calibrated measurement tool; precise tolerance values should be verified with dedicated measurement instruments before use in manufacturing.
